What Sharpwise does

Everything in the first list is in the game now, free, with nothing to install. The second list is what we are working towards next.

In the game today

Missions
Every topic is a mission of five waves that get harder as they go, with lives to keep and up to three stars to win.
Sky Storm
An endless storm of mixed questions that speeds up the longer a child keeps going, with Hammer Man's TNT bubbles to avoid.
Ninja Sprint
Sixty seconds to slice as many right answers as possible, with no lives to lose.
Boss Battle
Right answers knock down Hammer Man's health bar until he is out.
Ninja Duel
Two players share one device and one question, and the first right slice wins the round.
Memory Match
A calm card game of finding matching pairs, with no slicing.
Train with Sensei
Sensei picks the topics a child finds hardest and puts them into one practice session.
Letter tracing
Reception children trace letters with a finger, starting with the ones they learn to read first.
Daily Dojo
Three new challenges every day, with bonus coins and a streak for coming back.
Tables Check practice
Year 4 practice with the same timing as the multiplication tables check: 25 questions, 6 seconds each.
Arithmetic practice
Year 6 practice in the style of the arithmetic paper: ten questions, at the paper's own pace.
Statutory spelling lists
Every word on the statutory Year 3–4 and Year 5–6 spelling lists.
Coins and the Ninja Shop
Right answers earn coins, which buy new slice trails in the Ninja Shop.
Sticker album
Stickers of the ninjas and Hammer Man fill an album as coins add up and a child tries new topics, bosses and years.
Certificates
Winning a mission makes a certificate to print or share, and every certificate is kept in an album.
Belts and trophies
Ninja belts grow with the stars earned across every topic, and each topic has a bronze, silver or gold trophy to win in Ninja Sprint.
Four children, one device
Up to four children can each have their own ninja and their own progress on one phone, tablet or computer.
The grown-ups' area
Behind a quick sum, grown-ups see questions answered, accuracy, stars and the topics a child finds hardest.
Progress report
Grown-ups can share a short progress summary as text or as a one-page picture.
Read aloud
Questions can be read aloud, so children who cannot read yet can still play.
Slower bubbles and extra time
Grown-ups can slow the bubbles down, and give extra time or no time limit on timed questions.
Whiteboard mode
For a class at the front of the room: slower bubbles, questions read aloud, practice with no lives, and nothing saved.
Reception to Year 6
Seven islands, one for each school year from Reception to Year 6, each with maths and English topics.
Plays offline and installs
After the first visit it plays without a connection, and it can be added to the home screen like an app.
Move to another device
A save code carries a child's progress to another phone, tablet or computer.
No adverts, no tracking
No adverts, no analytics and no account: progress is kept on the device.

Coming later

These are plans, not promises, and none of them has a date.

Sharpwise on Google Play
An Android app in the Google Play store, made for families.
Sharpwise on the App Store
An app for iPhone and iPad.
A recorded voice
A real recorded voice for the game's everyday phrases, in place of the device's computer voice.
Celebration poses
Each ninja celebrating a win in a pose of its own.
A 3-D Sky Map
The Sky Map as floating 3-D islands.
Schools and classes
A way for a teacher to set up a class for the children to join.
